The Diagonal and the Log-Jacobian of a Map

Source: R/distrib_penalty.R
dp_diag_entries.Rd

dp_diag_entries() returns the entries of a Matrix diagonal map, including the zeros, and NULL for any other map. map_log_jacobian() returns \(\log\lvert\det D\rvert\): 0 for a NULL map, \(\sum_j\log\lvert d_j\rvert\) for a diagonal one, the log-modulus of the determinant for a square nonsingular one, and NA for a map that is not square or is singular. dp_log_jacobian() returns the same quantity for a built penalty.

Usage

dp_diag_entries(map)

map_log_jacobian(map)

dp_log_jacobian(penalty)

Arguments

map

The map \(D\): NULL, a base matrix or a Matrix.

penalty

A DistribPenalty() object.

Value

dp_diag_entries() returns a numeric vector of length nrow(map), a unit diagonal (diag = "U") giving ones, or NULL. map_log_jacobian() and dp_log_jacobian() return a single number, possibly NA.

Details

A diagonal map is treated as singular when an entry is zero or missing. Any other square map is converted once to a dense matrix; it is treated as singular when an entry is not finite or when the rank that qr() reports at its default tolerance is below the number of columns, and otherwise the log-modulus comes from determinant().

dp_log_jacobian() recomputes the quantity from the entries of a diagonal map, at the cost of \(q\) logarithms, so that the result stays correct when a caller replaces the map with a subset of its diagonal through S7::set_props() and the stored property is out of date. For any other map it reads the stored log_jacobian.

See also

distrib_penalty(), penalty_value.DistribPenalty()
